adjudication.rationale: In SalesforceCalendarService, the refreshed token is parsed via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then persisted as `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which (a) does not include required Salesforce fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `scope`, etc., and (b) as a `z.object(...)` will strip unknown keys by default. Therefore in “sharing mode” the persisted credential key can lose `instance_url` (and other non-minimum fields), which would plausibly break subsequent jsforce usage that relies on those fields being present in the stored credential.
